system_overview: This specification models a multi-car elevator system in a building with multiple floors. Multiple elevators service requests from people who wish to travel between floors. The specification includes a simple dispatch algorithm that selects the closest available elevator to service each call, and temporal properties ensure that every call is eventually serviced and every waiting person eventually reaches their destination.
actors_and_components: The system has three types of actors: (1) People, who decide on destination floors, call elevators, enter and exit elevators. (2) Elevators, which move between floors, open and close doors, and carry people. (3) A dispatcher that assigns elevators to service floor calls based on proximity. Each person has a location (either a floor or inside an elevator), a destination floor, and a waiting status. Each elevator has a current floor, a direction of travel (up, down, or stationary), a door state (open or closed), and a set of floor buttons that have been pressed by passengers inside.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) the state of each person, including their current location (a floor number or an elevator identifier), their desired destination floor, and whether they are currently waiting for an elevator; (2) a set of active elevator calls, where each call specifies a floor and a direction; (3) the state of each elevator, including its current floor, its direction of movement (up, down, or stationary), whether its doors are open, and the set of floor buttons pressed by its passengers.
initial_state: All people start on arbitrary floors with arbitrary destination floors. No person is waiting. There are no active elevator calls. All elevators start on arbitrary floors, stationary, with doors closed and no buttons pressed.
actions: The following actions can occur: (1) Pick new destination: a person who is not waiting and is on a floor chooses a new destination floor different from their current floor. (2) Call elevator: a person who is not waiting and whose destination differs from their location begins waiting and creates an elevator call for their floor and intended direction, unless an elevator is already at their floor going the right direction with doors open. (3) Open elevator doors: an elevator opens its doors if it is at a floor with a matching active call or a pressed button for that floor, clearing the corresponding call and button. (4) Enter elevator: all people waiting on the elevator's floor who are traveling in the elevator's direction enter the elevator, and their destination floor buttons are pressed. (5) Exit elevator: all passengers whose destination is the elevator's current floor exit onto that floor and stop waiting. (6) Close elevator doors: the elevator closes its doors once no one can enter or exit at the current floor. (7) Move elevator: the elevator moves one floor in its current direction, provided its doors are closed, it does not need to stop at the current floor, and any active call it could service is also coverable by another elevator. (8) Stop elevator: the elevator becomes stationary when it reaches the boundary floor and cannot continue in its current direction. (9) Dispatch elevator: when a call is active, the system selects the closest elevator that is either stationary or already approaching the call floor in the same direction, and directs it toward the call; a stationary elevator jumps directly to the call floor.
safety_properties: Type invariant: person states, elevator calls, and elevator states all conform to their expected types. Safety invariant: (1) an elevator has a floor button pressed only if some person inside that elevator is going to that floor; (2) if a person is inside a moving elevator, the elevator is moving toward that person's destination; (3) there are no ghost calls -- every active call has at least one person actually waiting at that floor for that direction.
liveness_properties: Every elevator call is eventually serviced by some elevator arriving at the call floor moving in the requested direction. Every person who is waiting for an elevator eventually arrives at their destination floor.
model_bounds: The set of people, the set of elevators, and the number of floors are declared as constants. Typical small model-checking configurations use 2 people, 2 elevators, and 2 floors. Medium configurations might use more people or floors.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for calling elevators, opening doors, entering elevators, exiting elevators, and stopping elevators. Strong fairness is assumed for closing doors, moving elevators, and dispatching elevators. The dispatch algorithm is simple and does not optimize for global throughput or average wait time -- it merely picks the closest eligible elevator. People may nondeterministically choose new destination floors at any time when not waiting.
